title: Microsoft Teams: keypad consent for recording and transcription in one-to-one PSTN calls
summary: Hold: the default-state label describes opting into the existing policy, not the new experience arriving for people already covered by it. The audit UI reference does not document the complete path printed in the table, and the audit guidance should acknowledge Microsoft's differing instructions for recorded or transcribed calls.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-10-23T21:59:27.
Teams plans keypad consent for recording and transcription for PSTN participants in one-to-one calls requiring explicit consent.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams will support explicit consent for participants connected through the public switched telephone network (PSTN) in one-to-one calls.

claims.claim: Where explicit consent is required, the PSTN participant hears an audio prompt when recording or transcription starts.
claims.quote: When explicit consent is required, PSTN participants will hear an audio prompt when recording or transcription is started.

claims.claim: A PSTN participant who declines can remain in the call but stays muted.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft's notice says rollout begins in early December 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026

claims.claim: The notice metadata gives 30 June 2027 as Microsoft's end date.
claims.quote: Microsoft's end date 2027-06-30

claims.claim: The supplied notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: The new keypad experience has default state admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: No new policy configuration is required if your existing explicit consent configuration meets your organization's requirements. [...] If explicit consent is already enabled, prepare users and support teams for the new PSTN keypad consent experience.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to "on": this is an automatic extension for calls already covered by the existing consent policy, not a new opt-in control. Retain the existing qualification that the underlying consent policy is disabled by default and that only calls requiring consent get the new prompt.

claims.claim: The consent setting is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Edit > Require participant agreement for recording and transcription.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. [...] Select the policy or policies that you want to modify, and then select Edit. [...] Require participant agreement for recording and transcription

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell documents Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExplicitRecordingConsent <string> for call consent, subject to the stated release warning.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy [...] [-Identity] <string> [...] [-ExplicitRecordingConsent <string>] [...] This setting controls whether users must provide or obtain explicit consent before recording a 1:1 PSTN or Teams call.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: No separate PSTN-only or keypad-only consent control is documented in either the admin UI or PowerShell.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN one-to-one explicit recording consent keypad license Teams Phone PSTN-only policy ExplicitRecordingConsent; "PSTN" "consent" "policy" "only". Read calling-policy and call-recording pages and Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy; only the shared consent setting was documented.

claims.claim: Call recording permission is controlled at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Cloud recording for calling.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. [...] Select the policy that you want to edit. [...] Turn Cloud recording for calling to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true enables call recording for the global policy, separately from consent.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables call recording for the global policy: [...] Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowCloudRecordingForCalls $true

claims.claim: Call transcription permission is controlled at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: select Voice > Calling policies. [...] Select the policy you want to modify. [...] Turn Transcription to On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true enables transcription for the global policy, separately from consent.
claims.quote: For example, this script enables transcription for the global policy: [...] Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true

claims.claim: The cited audit-search page documents Audit > Search > Activities - friendly names > Added information about call participants.
claims.quote: Searched: opened audit-search in full for Added information about call participants; it documents Audit, Search and Activities - friendly names, but not that final activity. The activity is stated on call-recording-transcription-captions and audit-log-activities instead.
claims.fix: Shorten controls[4].ui.path and its rendered table path to "Audit > Search > Activities - friendly names", retaining the audit-search docs URL. The named activity can remain in the explanatory prose supported by the already cited call-recording and audit-activities pages, with the source disagreement noted separately.

claims.where: controls[4].api; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <start date> -EndDate <end date> -Operations CallParticipantDetail searches the call-participant activity recommended by the call-recording page for consent data.
claims.quote: The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation. [...] For a list of the available values for this parameter, see Audited activities.

claims.where: controls[0].scope and note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Calling policies govern users and can differ between users through policy assignment.
claims.quote: You can use the global (Org-wide default) policy that's created automatically or create and assign custom policies. [...] You can assign a policy directly to users, either individually or at scale through a batch assignment

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy reference warns that ExplicitRecordingConsent has not been released and changing it has no effect, despite other sources describing an existing setting.
claims.quote: This feature has not been released yet and will have no changes if it is enabled or disabled.

claims.claim: The Disabled value means users are not required to obtain explicit consent before recording starts.
claims.quote: Disabled: Users are not required to obtain explicit consent before recording starts.

claims.claim: The call-recording Learn page describes a Yes or No consent prompt for call participants.
claims.quote: When a participant decides to un-mute, turn on their camera, or share content, they're asked to respond 'Yes' or 'No' to consent to be included in the recording and transcription.

claims.claim: The ExplicitRecordingConsent calling-policy parameter covers both Teams one-to-one VoIP and PSTN calls, rather than only PSTN calls.
claims.quote: This parameter manages recording consent for Teams 1:1 VoIP and PSTN calls.

claims.claim: Audio Conferencing and group calls are managed by the Teams meeting policy instead.
claims.quote: Audio conferencing and group calls are managed by Teams Meeting Policy.

claims.claim: The meeting-consent Learn page currently lists PSTN endpoints in one-to-one calls as auto-consented, unlike the planned keypad experience.
claims.quote: The following user types are auto consented for recording and transcription without any participant interaction. [...] PSTN endpoints in 1:1 calls

claims.claim: The call-recording Learn page says each participant's consent choice is visible to an admin and included in the call's Purview audit log.
claims.quote: The consent choice for each participant is visible by the admin and is included in the Purview audit log for the call.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the planned one-to-one PSTN keypad prompt at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN keypad consent 1 2 ExplicitRecordingConsent separate policy audit CallParticipantDetail. Read call-recording and participant-agreement pages; results describe client Yes/No, 1:1 PSTN auto consent, or Audio Conferencing keypad controls, not this planned 1:1 PSTN prompt.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the planned PSTN keypad choices are logged under the same activity as existing call consent data.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams PSTN keypad consent 1 2 ExplicitRecordingConsent separate policy audit CallParticipantDetail; "PSTN" "keypad" "consent" "audit". Read call-recording, participant-agreement, audit activities and MC1530950; no passage specifies logging of the planned keypad choice.

claims.claim: The existing call-recording Learn page says explicit consent is unsupported for call queue calls.
claims.quote: Explicit consent is not supported for call queue calls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not separately explain call queue applicability for the planned PSTN keypad capability.
claims.quote: Searched: "PSTN" "consent" "call queue". Read call-recording-transcription-captions and MC1530950; the former states the existing call queue limitation, while neither explicitly describes call queue treatment for the planned keypad extension.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor MC1530950 names a licence, meter or charge for the capability.
claims.quote: Searched: read supplied roadmap description and MC1530950 in full for licence, license, meter and charge; neither names a licensing requirement or price for this capability.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Capability-specific licensing is not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown rather than asserted to be included.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams explicit consent recording transcription calling license requirements Teams Phone. Read calling-policy, call-recording and Teams add-on licensing pages. General Teams Phone/PSTN licensing is published, but no separate licensing terms for the planned keypad extension were found.

claims.claim: The calling-policies Learn page describes the consent setting without naming a licence for that setting.
claims.quote: Searched: read teams-calling-policy in full for licensing of Require participant agreement for recording and transcription. The page lists the setting and explains policy creation, editing and assignment, but names no licence for it.

claims.claim: The notice describes responding by phone keypad without describing a sign-in step.
claims.quote: PSTN participants will hear an audio prompt requesting consent when recording or transcription starts.- Participants can press 1 to consent or 2 to decline.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is the audit-search cmdlet and is run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. [...] You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Added information about call participants is the friendly name for the CallParticipantDetail operation.
claims.quote: Added information about call participants ^10, 11, 12^ | CallParticipantDetail | Teams added information about the participants of a call

claims.claim: The sources describe no autonomous behaviour for this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: read roadmap description, MC1530950 and call-recording-transcription-captions for autonomous actions. They describe a prompt triggered by recording or transcription, the participant's response and policy enforcement, not an autonomous agent.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The call-recording page directs administrators to the Added information about call participants filter for consent data.
claims.quote: You can view consent data using the Added information about call participants filter in the Teams calling audit logs in Purview.
claims.fix: Append this qualification to the audit guidance and controls[4].note: "The call-recording page directs admins to Added information about call participants, but the audit activities reference says calls that are recorded or transcribed are included in MeetingParticipantDetail." Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-activities for that qualification; do not present CallParticipantDetail as an undisputed filter for recorded calls.
